_meta.purpose: The closed VALIDATED tag vocabulary every item seed entry draws `tags` from (seed-contract.md §2.1, §8). Consumed by ~125 parallel authoring agents across base types, uniques, sets, and affix families. An unknown tag id rejects at import.
_meta.immutability: FROZEN v1 once an owner flips `frozen` to true and authoring begins against it. Unlike `core.v1.json`'s rarity ladder and role list, this vocabulary is NOT append-only even before freezing — it is a fixed, deliberately-sized set for the whole v1 corpus. Adding, renaming, or removing a tag id is a v2 event that requires an explicit owner re-run decision (seed-contract.md §7.3), never an in-place edit of this file.
_meta.closedVocabularyNote: Authors NAME a tag; they do not MINT one (seed-contract.md §2, the VALIDATED ownership level). A seed file that references a tag id not listed below fails import with an unknown-tag reason code. Do not add a tag 'just in case' — see designNotes.cutRationale for what was already turned away and why.
_meta.idGrammarNote: Tag ids and axis ids are lowercase-kebab. `nameKey` follows seed-contract.md §6: `^[a-z0-9.-]+$`, pattern `tag.<axis>.<id>`.
_meta.oneAxisPerEntryRule: For an axis marked `exclusive: true`, a single entry may carry at most one tag from that axis. The validator enforces this per axis, not across the whole `tags` array — an entry may freely combine one tag from `mass-class` with one from `material-nature`, etc. Axes marked `exclusive: false` (`economy-source`) allow zero, one, or more of that axis's values on the same entry.
_meta.appliesToNote: `appliesTo` on each axis is authoring guidance, not an enforced constraint in this file — it tells an author which entry shapes (seed-contract.md §10) the axis is meaningful for. A physical-property axis like `mass-class` has nothing to say about an affix family, which is not itself a physical object.
sourceRefs: data/seed/items/_registry/core.v1.json (rarity/roles/categories — a different registry, not duplicated here)
data/seed/items/_registry/themes.v1.json (named flavor-worlds — a different registry, not duplicated here)

designNotes.targetCountRationale: Seven axes, nineteen tags. Small enough that one author can hold the whole vocabulary in working memory while filling in a base type, large enough that the four formulas named in seed-contract.md §8 that read tags (weight, durability, vendor stock, loot filters) each get a real, distinguishable input instead of one overloaded 'flavor' string. Every axis maps to a formula or system named in this repo's own docs — none were added speculatively to round out a category list.

cutRationale.candidate: bulk (a second physical-size axis alongside mass-class)
cutRationale.reason: No consumer distinct from the weight/encumbrance formula that mass-class already feeds (seed-contract.md §8). Two axes driving the same formula the same way is not two signals, it is one signal with double the chance of disagreeing with itself.

Fully covered by material-nature=organic plus origin=rooted. No system was found that needs 'fungal' distinguished from 'floral' distinguished from generic organic-and-rooted; adding them would only fragment the loot-filter/vendor-stock grouping the origin axis exists to feed.

Duplicates the DERIVED `stock_eligible` flag (ssot-inventory.md — computed structurally from pool_rolls=0 and Fixed-only implicits). An authored 'starter' tag could silently disagree with that computed truth; the derivation is already the single source.

No named consumer in seed-contract.md, enrichment-contract.md, or any of the four SSOT docs read for this task. 'Which items are chase items' is a curation/marketing question with no formula or system currently planned to read it — SC7's 'not content, it is a lie in a table' applies directly.

seed-contract.md §8 states salvage yield's inputs explicitly: rarity band, ilvl, enhancement level. Tags are not among them. A tag whose only plausible formula names inputs that exclude it has zero declared reader.

Redundant with the entry's own VALIDATED `element`/`variants` field (seed-contract.md §10's affix-family example already carries `variants.generate: elements+omni`). A second, unenforced tag saying the same thing can drift out of sync with the field a formula would actually read.

leastCertain: notability=signature — the weakest-supported tag here. Its consumer (a loot-filter highlight bucket / balance-review curation queue) is plausible but, unlike the other six axes, is not named or evidenced anywhere in the four SSOT docs; it is inferred from the seed-contract.md §10 unique example, which already tags a unique 'signature'. Kept because cutting it would make that worked example in the binding contract doc unauthorable, but it should be the first axis re-examined if a reviewer wants to shrink v1 further.

economy-source=crafted-only / vendor-stocked — real per seed-contract.md §8's 'vendor stock · loot filters · market value' formula row, but that row's current planned consumers (I3 vendor rotation, I12 drop tables) are both unbuilt. The tag is sound; the systems that would read it are further out than the other five axes' consumers.

origin (rooted / undead / mechanical) — deliberately kept narrow to avoid re-deriving `themes.v1.json`'s named flavor-worlds or overlapping material-nature's organic/necrotic/metal substance axis. The line between 'origin flavor' and 'material substance' is a real design cut, not an obvious one, and a reviewer could reasonably argue origin should be folded into material-nature instead of standing alone.

axes.definition: How much physical mass or bulk this entry reads as carrying on a body.
axes.v3Note: Widened from three values to five after the pilot. TWO independent agents on two different partitions each invented the rung they needed — medium-heavy on a plant armour band, medium-light on a humanoid weapon band. When separate authors who cannot see each other reach for the same missing value, the vocabulary is too coarse, not the authors careless. A weapon ladder and an armour ladder both span more than three perceptible weights. Additive: light/medium/heavy keep their exact meaning, so nothing authored under v1 or v2 becomes invalid.

axes.definition: What the entry is physically made of, at the coarsest level a formula needs.
How the entry wears relative to what its class and rarity alone would predict.
The entry's primary tactical intent, orthogonal to its equip role.
axes.v2Note: Extended wave 0c after the pilot. A gem partition tagged its inserts offensive/defensive and was rejected, with no alternative vocabulary offered — the powerCategories vector is a different thing (it prices an effect; this groups an item for filters and vendor stock). This axis stated its own consumers as vendor-stock and loot-filter grouping, and gems, charms and consumables are all filterable inventory. Excluding them was an oversight, not a rule.

axes.definition: The entry's biological/thematic origin — independent of what it is physically made of (material-nature) and independent of the named flavor-world it might belong to (themes.v1.json).
Which non-drop distribution channels this entry is meant to be reachable through. Not mutually exclusive — an entry can be neither, either, or both.
Flags an entry as a hand-picked standout among its peers, for curation and display — never a power claim.

tags.definition: Occupies no meaningful mass or bulk on the body — cloth-weight, papery, or effectively weightless. Two agents must agree: if you'd call it 'a few ounces' or lighter, it is light.

frozenNote: FROZEN v2. v1 excluded gem/charm/consumable from combat-posture; corrected after the pilot, before any partition consumed v1 except the pilot itself, which re-runs.
minCompatibleNote: v2 only WIDENED combat-posture.appliesTo to include gem/charm/consumable. Nothing legal under v1 became illegal, so v1-authored content stays valid.
v4Note: Widened four physical axes after stage 1a. A MATERIAL is the most natural thing in the corpus to carry material-nature, mass-class and durability-class — a shard is mineral, a substrate is organic or metal — yet appliesTo listed only base-type and unique. The axes were written before the material kind had a shape, so the omission is an oversight rather than a rule. Additive: nothing legal before became illegal.
stage1aFrozen: Stage 1a authored and validated at 0 errors (205 entries, 25 files). From here a change to this registry invalidates authored content unless minCompatibleVersion says otherwise.
